title: Wall Street Banks Turn More Upbeat on Global Growth Following Iran Deal
detail: Investment banks turned more optimistic on the global economic outlook in the weeks following the Iran deal. JPMorgan's chief economist wrote that the deal, cooling trade-war rhetoric, and a tech-capex surge were laying the groundwork for 'a period of strong and balanced global growth.' No specific revised numeric JPMorgan recession-probability figure was published alongside the commentary — the firm's most recent hard number remained its pre-deal estimate — but the tonal shift across major banks marked a meaningful change from the stagflation-trap narrative that had dominated the spring.
